channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar remains subdued as US Dollar gains on renewed Hormuz tensions
item.description: NZD/USD inches lower for the second successive day, trading around 0.5700 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The currency pair depreciates as the US Dollar (USD) holds ground, which could be attributed to the renewed geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Gold declines as reviving inflation fears outweigh receding Fed rate hike bets and soft USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) attracts sellers for the second straight day and drops to the $4,125-$4,124 region during the Asian session on Tuesday. Crude oil prices edge higher amid renewed tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, reviving inflationary concerns.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Eases from two-week top; 38.2% Fibo. near 0.6955 holds the key
item.description: The AUD/USD retreats slightly from the 0.6960 area, or a two-week high, touched during the Asian session on Tuesday, and, for now, seems to have snapped a three-day winning streak.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices fell in India on Tuesday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD corrects further to near $61 as oil prices attract bids
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is down 1.35% to near $61.00 during the Asian trading session on Tuesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen strengthens amid looming intervention risks; lacks bullish conviction
item.description: The USD/JPY pair extends the previous day's late pullback from the vicinity of mid-162.00s and attracts some follow-through sellers during the Asian session on Tuesday.

item.title: WTI rises above $69.00 as Iran strikes commercial vessels in Hormuz
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price gains ground after registering modest losses in the previous day, trading around $69.20 per barrel during the Asian hours on Tuesday. Crude oil prices receive a temporary boost following renewed geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Japan’s Kiuchi: Tokyo is not easing fiscal discipline, presenting it clearly in the economic plan
item.description: Minoru Kiuchi, Minister of State for Economic and Fiscal Policy of Japan, said on Tuesday that “Tokyo is not easing fiscal discipline, presenting it clearly in the economic plan.”

item.title: Iran strikes commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Bloomberg carried a story by an Axios reporter late Monday, citing a US official, that Iran fired at least two missiles at commercial ships transiting through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: British Pound gains as easing Fed hike bets weigh on US Dollar
item.description: GBP/USD continues its winning streak for the ninth consecutive day, trading around 1.3390 during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.8054 vs. 6.8066 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Tuesday at 6.8054 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.8066 and 6.7838 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Euro extends the range play above 1.1400 as Hormuz risks support USD
item.description: The EUR/USD pair extends its sideways consolidative price move during the Asian session on Tuesday, though it manages to hold comfortably above the 1.1400 mark. Moreover, spot prices remain well within striking distance of a nearly two-week high, touched last Thursday.

item.title: Australian Dollar declines as ANZ–Indeed Job Ads drop in June
item.description: AUD/USD inches lower after two days of gains, trading around 0.6950 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. The Australian Dollar (AUD) faces downward pressure as weakening economic sentiment amid a cooling labor market signals that high borrowing costs are taking a toll.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Rallies and hits 18-year highs above 217.00
item.description: The British Pound rallies to an 18-year high against the Japanese Yen, registering solid gains of over 0.77% as the GBP/JPY clears the previous year-to-date (YTD) high of 216.60 as the cross-pair clears the 217.00 figure for the first time since January 2008.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rally stalls, sellers eye $60.00
item.description: Silver price retreats by over 1% on Monday, even as the Greenback and US Treasury yields edge lower, with the white metal threatening to drop below $60 for the first time this week. At the time of writing, the XAG/USD trades at $61.80, after peaking at around $63.28 earlier during the day,

item.title: Japanese Yen finds the line in the sand is mostly sand
item.description: USD/JPY spent Monday doing what it has done for most of the year, grinding higher while officialdom watched.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Range trade persists against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes USD/SGD has seen downward momentum slow after last week’s sharp drop, with the pair expected to stay between 1.2900 and 1.2935 intraday. On a 1–3 week horizon, UOB maintains a neutral stance, projecting consolidation within 1.2890–1.2990.

item.title: Pound Sterling rallies into its own coronation
item.description: GBP/USD has quietly put together eight consecutive higher daily closes, a grind from near 1.3150 that has delivered the pair directly onto its 200-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA), with the 50-day EMA just beneath it and the 1.3400 handle immediately overhead.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar stays neutral as Fed’s Waller reinforces inflation commitment
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) remains neutral near the 100.90 level at the end of the American session on Monday as investors digest hawkish comments from Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller and resilient United States (US) services data.

item.title: Australian Dollar rises as softer Fed bets offset resilient US data
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) extends its rally into a third straight trading session, up 0.25% on Monday, as investors adjust their interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve (Fed) following a soft US jobs report last week.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Depressed positioning offers re-entry – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu stresses that Chinese equities and Chinese Yuan (CNY) remain heavily under-owned versus APAC (Asia-Pacific) peers, with cross-border holdings at very low levels.

item.title: Indonesia: Deficit raises external risk questions – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kunal Kundu analyzes Indonesia’s May 2026 trade data, highlighting the first deficit since the pandemic and a record Oil and Gas shortfall.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar pressured by hawkish Fed tone
item.description: NZD/USD trades under pressure near the 0.5700 level as the US Dollar (USD) remains supported by hawkish-leaning comments from Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller and resilient United States (US) services data.

item.title: Gold slips as firm US yields cap post-NFP rebound
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price retreats by some 0.50% on Monday as the Greenback remains steady despite traders repricing a less hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) following last Thursday’s softer-than-expected jobs report. The XAU/USD pair trades at $4,153, down 0.50%.

item.title: United States Dollar Index trims gains as Fed hike bets fade
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) trims its gains on Monday after opening the week on a firmer note, as traders await greater clarity on the Federal Reserve's (Fed) interest rate path before placing fresh directional bets.

item.title: Crude Oil runs out of war and out of buyers
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) has spent three weeks handing back what the war spent three months building, and the tape now reads as though February never ended.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Hawkish RBNZ risks and range trading – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s FX Strategy team discusses the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) ahead of the July 8 Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) meeting, where consensus and the bank expect a 25 bp hike to 2.5%.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average makes history, then thinks better of it
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) finally crossed 53,000 on Monday, spiking to a record just above the handle in the opening minutes and holding it for roughly the length of the ceremony that produced it.

item.title: Gold consolidates below $4,200 as traders reassess Fed interest rate outlook
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) consolidates losses on Monday as a firmer US Dollar (USD) and mild profit-taking cap gains following last week's rebound from a more than seven-month low of $3,941.

item.title: Swiss Franc dips amid unemployment surprise and strong US Dollar
item.description: USD/CHF gains 0.37% on Monday, trading around 0.8060 at the time of writing, as the US Dollar (USD) rebounds despite slightly softer expectations for further monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve (Fed).
